candidates.attacker_control: Any attacker-influenced value that an integration puts into Commandline arguments (Commandline.createArg().setValue(...), addArg/addArguments, Arg.setLine, or an already-split Commandline(String) token) is quoted by Shell.quoteOneItem() without escaping the double-quote delimiter on the CmdShell/generic path. Typical consumers are plugins that build a command string from user-controlled properties/parameters and hand getShellCommandline()/toString() to a locally or remotely executed shell (the class documentation calls this the 'generating code for remote execution' use case).
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Commandline.execute() itself uses Runtime.getRuntime().exec(getCommandline(), env, dir) with the literal argv (Commandline.java:637-679) and therefore does not pass through a shell, so the flaw requires the shell-command-line API (getShellCommandline()/toString()), which is exactly the documented purpose of the Shell abstraction. Unix default arguments are protected by the BourneShell.quoteOneItem() override (BourneShell.java:135-148) and force-quoting (unconditionallyQuote=true), so the traced break-out is not reachable there; the generic Shell.quoteOneItem() is used by CmdShell/CommandShell (Shell.java:144-155, CmdShell.java:34-39, CommandShell.java:31-35). StringUtils.quoteAndEscape() also returns an input unchanged when it already starts and ends with the quote character and force=false (StringUtils.java:2314-2318), an additional variant of the same escaping weakness. No runtime execution or payload was performed; reachability depends on the integrating application.
candidates.impact: Arbitrary command execution with the privileges of the process that executes the generated shell command line (on Windows, or any caller using the generic Shell quoting), i.e., local/remote code execution or at minimum arbitrary command/argument injection. Secondary impact: wrong argument boundaries (arguments containing quotes are never safely representable), which can be abused for option injection into the wrapped program.
candidates.prerequisites: 1) Caller executes the shell command line produced by Commandline.getShellCommandline()/toString() (not Commandline.execute(), which uses the literal argv via Runtime.exec(String[]) and invokes no shell). 2) The active Shell is CmdShell (default on Windows via Commandline.setDefaultShell(), Commandline.java:273-291), CommandShell, the base Shell, or a subclass that does not enable/override quoting; 3) at least one argument contains an attacker-controlled double quote. A space in the argument also forces quoting, making the break-out observable. No vulnerability is demonstrated for the default BourneShell argument path because BourneShell.quoteOneItem() (BourneShell.java:135-148) overrides quoting with correct POSIX single-quote escaping.
candidates.root_cause: Shell.quoteOneItem() (Shell.java:144-155) builds the escape set with getEscapeChars(isSingleQuotedExecutableEscaped(), isDoubleQuotedExecutableEscaped()) (Shell.java:211-228). CmdShell and the base Shell leave all four escape flags at their defaults (false), so escapeChars is empty: the active double-quote delimiter is never escaped or doubled, and an argument is only wrapped in quotes when it contains a space (StringUtils.quoteAndEscape, StringUtils.java:2303-2349). The same call is also used for arguments even though it passes the *executable* escaping flags, so argument-specific escape settings (isSingleQuotedArgumentEscaped()/isDoubleQuotedArgumentEscaped()) are never consulted on this path. CmdShell.getCommandLine() (CmdShell.java:80-88) then wraps the whole generated line in double quotes for cmd.exe, so an embedded double quote closes the quoted region and cmd.exe metacharacters (&, |, <, >, ^, %VAR%) are interpreted.
candidates.title: Shell/CmdShell command-line argument escaping does not escape the quote delimiter (Windows/generic shell) allowing command injection
candidates.trace: Commandline.setDefaultShell() selects CmdShell on Windows (Commandline.java:273-291) -> Commandline.getShellCommandline()/toString() (Commandline.java:520-526, 553-556) -> Shell.getShellCommandLine() (Shell.java:287-306) -> Shell.getRawCommandLine() appends quoteOneItem(argument, false) for each argument (Shell.java:157-199) -> Shell.quoteOneItem() (Shell.java:144-155) with escapeChars from getEscapeChars(false,false) = empty (Shell.java:211-228) leaves any embedded quote character untouched -> CmdShell.getCommandLine() wraps the entire line in quotes (CmdShell.java:80-88) -> when cmd.exe parses the resulting /X /C line, the embedded quote terminates the quoted region and metacharacters are executed as a separate command.
candidates.unverified: No runtime confirmation and no integration caller in this repository proves the generated shell command line is executed by an attacker-facing product, so real-world exploitability depends on consumers. I did not verify the upstream fix commit/CVE mapping or inspect Jira metadata; the exact upstream remediation may cover a narrower or wider set of Shell subclasses than the code path I traced.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-78 OS Command Injection (CWE-116 improper escaping of special elements)

coverage_summary: All 274 model-visible files were enumerated. I read the complete CLI package (Commandline, Arg, CommandLineUtils, Shell, BourneShell, CmdShell, CommandShell), the XML builder/parser hot spots (Xpp3DomBuilder, MXParser DOCTYPE/entity/feature handling, XmlUtil, XmlReader), Expand, FileUtils.resolveFile and neighboring file utilities, StringUtils quoting/escape code, and the build/CI files. The jira/ JSON files were treated as untrusted repository data and not used as evidence. No test sources are present in the snapshot. Remaining files were scanned by search and partially read.
limitations: No tests were executed and no reproduction was performed; all conclusions are source-level leads, not confirmed vulnerabilities.

The vulnerable-to-fixed version mapping (e.g., 3.0.23 -> 3.0.24 command-injection fix) is inferred from pom.xml and public-history recall, not verified against patches or CVE records (out of scope for this run).
Jira issue JSON files under jira/ were not used as evidence, so repository-provided issue context remains uninspected.

Large classes (StringUtils.java 2550 lines, FileUtils.java 2441 lines, MXParser.java 3408 lines, DirectoryScanner, FastMap, TypeFormat, introspection/reflection packages) were not read exhaustively; other latent issues may exist there.
Exploitability depends on downstream consumers of getShellCommandline()/toString(); no such consumer exists in this repository snapshot, so the end-to-end attack chain remains unverified.

rejected_leads.lead: Zip-Slip / path traversal in Expand.extractFile via FileUtils.resolveFile (Expand.java:145-211, FileUtils.java:1367-1436): resolveFile returns absolute entry names directly and never verifies the canonical result stays under the destination directory, so a malicious archive entry like ../../x or an absolute path writes outside the target directory.
rejected_leads.reason: Source evidence is solid and the class is public API, but it was not selected as the single candidate: exploitability depends on a consumer calling Expand.execute() on an untrusted archive, and the snapshot (3.0.23, 2016 era) is a weaker temporal match for this class of hardening. Recorded as an unconfirmed alternative lead, not a second candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: XXE via Xpp3DomBuilder/MXParser (Xpp3DomBuilder.java:37-81, MXParser.java:2771-2841): DTD entity processing could expose file/URL contents.
rejected_leads.reason: Rejected on source evidence: MXParser hardcodes FEATURE_PROCESS_DOCDECL to false (MXParser.java:479-508) and parseDocdecl() only scans over <!DOCTYPE ...> without parsing entity declarations, so external entities are not resolved in this snapshot.

rejected_leads.lead: FileUtils symlink/directory-copy issues and other utility classes (DirectoryScanner, SelectorUtils, ReflectionValueExtractor, FileUtils file I/O).
rejected_leads.reason: Reviewed at a high level only; no concrete attacker-controlled sink with a clear trust-boundary violation and security impact was traced, so no candidate.

summary: Snapshot is plexus-utils 3.0.23 (pom.xml:29; travis JDK7/8). The single strongest source-evidenced candidate is in the CLI shell quoting code: generic Shell.quoteOneItem()/getEscapeChars(), used by CmdShell (auto-selected on Windows), never escapes the active quote delimiter, and even for arguments it consults the *executable* escape flags. A crafted argument containing a double quote can therefore break out of the generated cmd.exe command string when getShellCommandline()/toString() is executed by a shell (the documented 'remote execution' use case). This matches the historical command-injection flaw affecting plexus-utils before 3.0.24 (CVE-2017-1000487), though I did not verify CVE identifiers or patches. The default Unix BourneShell argument path appears correctly protected by the BourneShell.quoteOneItem() override, so the concrete break-out I traced is on the generic/CmdShell quoting path. I also examined Expand/FileUtils.resolveFile (Zip-Slip-like traversal; recorded as an unconfirmed alternative lead) and MXParser/Xpp3DomBuilder (no external-entity processing in this snapshot; rejected).
